about.headline: Final-year CSE student in Dhaka, building the kind of machine learning that can *explain itself*.
paragraphs: The way I work is unglamorous. A question becomes a notebook, the notebook becomes a repo, and the repo becomes something a person can actually click. I would rather ship a rough version that works this week than a perfect plan that never leaves the doc.

It started as web development — complex designs, critical situations, things that had to work in front of users. It ended up in research papers on deepfake detection and chatbots for mental health. Same job either way: build something that holds up when a person depends on it.

skillsIntro: Straight off the CV: the languages I write, the front and back end I build with, the databases behind them, the AI/ML side, and the tools plus working habits that actually get a build out the door.

builds.title: SkillHub
builds.blurb:
A full-stack learning marketplace: mentors publish courses, learners find, buy and finish them in their own language, and an admin approves courses and runs the platform. Built from the 77-page SRS of our Software Engineering course project, with all 24 functional requirements implemented.

It includes SkillHub Match, a mentor-matching engine that explains its ranking, and SkillBot, an assistant that answers from the platform's live data. The interface comes in 8 languages, with a right-to-left layout for Arabic. Learners get email-OTP sign-up, simulated payments with PDF receipts, timed quizzes, assignments and a PDF certificate on completion.

Demo accounts for learner, mentor and admin are listed in the GitHub README.

builds.title: HireHub — Job Portal
builds.blurb:
A multi-role job portal: employers post jobs and move applicants through a hiring pipeline, recruiters place candidates for client companies, job seekers search and apply, and an admin moderates the platform. Use it per role (four portals) or as one platform with a single sign-in that works out who you are.

A three-person team project in plain PHP and MySQL, with MVC folders and AJAX filtering. I built the employer and recruiter modules and did the integration and security work (prepared statements, CSRF protection).

Demo accounts for every role are listed in the GitHub README.

builds.title: JobMatch-BD
builds.blurb:
Upload a CV, or fill in a short profile, and JobMatch BD ranks tech jobs in Bangladesh against it. Every result shows why it matched: the skills you have, the ones you're missing, and a score breakdown.

The score combines semantic similarity (sentence embeddings, so “neural networks” can match “deep learning”) with structured matching of skills, education, experience and location. It fetches live postings, keeps a shortlist, and can email a digest when new jobs score at least 50.

The API runs on a free server, so the first request after a quiet spell can take about a minute.

builds.title: Luffy — The Unknown Journey
builds.blurb:
A 2D story adventure for our Computer Graphics course: a boy named Luffy is pulled into the World of Chaos through his game console and has to cross five levels, each with a different kind of gameplay, to beat the Chaos King and get home. Play it in the browser.

Everything on screen is drawn with OpenGL shapes and every sound is generated in code: no images, sprites, sound files or game engine. It runs in the browser through WebAssembly. Techniques include particle systems, a radial torch-light mask, hierarchical modelling, projectile physics, and hand-written DDA line drawing and Cohen–Sutherland clipping.

A five-person team. I made the story, the title screen and cutscenes, and Level 1, the dungeon. The repository holds the playable build; the source code is private.

Fan project: the hero is a tribute to Luffy from One Piece (Eiichiro Oda).

builds.title: DevVault
builds.blurb: A Windows developer-environment assistant for the command line, written because cloning someone else's repository should not cost an hour of guessing. It reports whether the environment is ready, what kind of project a folder holds, which frameworks and dependencies it uses, where each dependency came from, whether any is declared twice, which local ports are busy, and what to install after a fresh clone.

builds.title: Zoo Management System
builds.blurb:
A desktop app that runs a whole zoo, built for the OOP-II course in C# WinForms on SQL Server: 47 screens over a 27-table database, with separate sides for admins, staff, doctors and visitors.

Visitors sign up with an email OTP, buy tickets and memberships, book events, shop, and pay through a built-in bank system that confirms each transaction with a one-time code. Staff get work schedules, their assigned animals and a live chat. Doctors run checkups, treatments and medical records. Admins manage animals, employees, members, visitors, events and status reports. There is also a map page for getting to the zoo and a video tour.

The point was to make the object model visible in something that actually runs.

builds.title: Shop Management System
builds.blurb: A shop-front exercise in Java: a customer browses laptops and phones and buys them while stock and sales move through the flow. Small on purpose — it was the course build for object-oriented modelling.

arenas.title: GridWise LLM
arenas.note: Built for the preliminary round as Team Byte Force: a public HTTP API that reads a campus operator's notes with Gemini, then hands the numbers to a PuLP optimiser and returns a cost-optimal 24-hour energy schedule. The model interprets the brief — it never gets to fake the arithmetic.

researchSummary: Three carry a decision already — one accepted and waiting on publication, two already presented. Four more are sitting with reviewers right now. Every entry below is one I can hand a question about.

research.title: Explainable and Generalizable Deepfake Detection for Vishing Attack Recognition
research.note: Voice-cloning attacks scored on ASVspoof and In-the-Wild with EER and AUC, plus SHAP explanations of what the model actually listened to. I-COSTE 2026: Sustainable Technology for Humanity and Global Impact.

research.title: Using Chatbots for Mental Health Support Among University Students in Bangladesh: An Exploratory Study
research.note: Abstract and poster on chatbot-supported mental health care for Bangladeshi university students, presented at the National Biomed Health ResearchCon held by Dhaka Medical College Research & Academic Club with Bangladesh Society of Medicine.

research.title: Transformational Leadership and Organizational Change in Bangladeshi Higher Education Institutions
research.note: With Protiti Sahajee Prachi and Md. Mortuza Ahmmed, on how leadership style shapes change inside Bangladeshi higher education. Presented at the 7th International Conference on Integrated Sciences, Eastern University, Dhaka.

research.title: PCOSNet: A Lightweight and Explainable Framework for Robust PCOS Detection
research.note: A small framework for PCOS detection, held to two demands at once: stay lightweight and stay explainable.

research.title: Ova-VSSM: VMamba-Inspired Lightweight Architecture for Multi-Class Ovarian Ultrasound Image Classification
research.note: A VMamba-inspired architecture doing multi-class classification on ovarian ultrasound images at a fraction of the usual weight.

research.title: Explainable Fake News Detection with Traditional Machine Learning: Evaluating Text Representations and Dataset Artifacts
research.note: Fake news detection without a large model: which text representation actually earns the accuracy, and how much of it is a dataset artifact.
